messages:
julie: FYI acme reported a spike of 429s on their dedicated pool starting ~09:30 PT. They have reserved capacity but are seeing sustained 429 + high tail latency. tenant_id=acme-123. Posting their minimal repro and headers below.

julie: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1715010200

julie: customer says their plan is supposed to allow 360k tokens/hour, not 100/s. They quoted UI numbers that don't match what we have in quota store. Can someone check per-tenant quota mapping & the dedicated pool routing?

ken: looking. I can see their reserved pool: pool=d-dedicated-east-1-42, capacity healthy. But ratekeys show per_tenant_ceiling=100 and denom="second" in the effective quota blob. That explains 100/s. Suspect migration script converted units to seconds for this tenant by mistake.

mina: autoscale logs around the same time show no new nodes added because the pool wasn't hitting node-level CPU/GPU thresholds — requests were being rejected at the rate limiter earlier. autoscale-bot events: 
```
autoscale-bot: [09:31:05] evaluated pool=d-dedicated-east-1-42, desired=10, actual=10
autoscale-bot: [09:31:30] no scale action: rate-limiter rejecting requests, not load-driven
```

ramiro: can you paste the quota blob from the config store? I want to confirm whether it's a global conversion or an isolated tenant bug.

ken: grabbing it now.
```
ken: select tenant_id, quota_value, quota_denom from tenant_quotas where tenant_id='acme-123';
-- result: tenant_id=acme-123, quota_value=100, quota_denom='second'
```

ken: other tenants in same cohort show denom='hour'. So it's an isolated miswrite during plan-migrate job earlier this week (job id 2024-04-12-plan-migrate).

julie: ok root cause identified: per-tenant quota denom incorrectly set to seconds which reduces allowed throughput by 3600x relative to intended hour denom. Impact: customers on dedicated pool hit 429s even though pool healthy.

mina: mitigation options: 1) change quota_denom back to 'hour' for acme-123 and invalidate quota cache; 2) temporarily bump per_tenant_ceiling to a safe value while we roll the permanent fix; 3) notify customer and apply a short-lived quota override. I can run the cache invalidation once DB change is applied.

ramiro: let's do a targeted DB patch + cache flush. Proposed patch:
```
UPDATE tenant_quotas SET quota_denom='hour' WHERE tenant_id='acme-123';
POST /internal/quota/cache/invalidate?tenant=acme-123
```
We'll also add a brief canary to make sure no ripple effects.

ken: I applied the DB change and posted the invalidate command. Watching logs.

jenkins-bot: [09:42] job quota-cache-flush/acme-123 succeeded

mina: after flush we should see immediate change in effective quota. Ken, can you show the limiter feedback headers now?

ken: re-ran the curl from earlier. Response now:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 360000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 359900
```
Looks good. No more 429s in the last 10m. Latency normalized.

julie: customer confirmed they no longer see 429 and app recovered. Sending a support note with explanation and apology. :white_check_mark:

ramiro: postmortem action items: 1) add validation to migration job to assert denom in {minute,hour,day} and convert units explicitly; 2) add a smoke test after plan-migrate which hits a sample tenant on dedicated pools and checks expected headers; 3) add alert when quota_denom != cohort-default for >1 tenant in a cohort.

ken: filed infra ticket INF-8345 and PR with migration validation linked.

mina: will write short runbook for oncall: how to inspect tenant quota blob, how to patch and flush cache, and how to apply temporary override.

julie: thanks all. I'll follow up with acme postmortem and close the escalation once runbook is published. :memo:
